bootstrap_stability.construct: mean ARI across bootstrap resamples of the whole fit (a global-fit stability score, not per-cluster)
bootstrap_stability.feasibility_note: requires Section 9.4's bootstrap_stability to have already run once on the full feature matrix
bootstrap_stability.min_sample_size: governed by phenotype_discovery.bootstrap_stability's own n_bootstrap, not this criterion
bootstrap_stability.unit_of_analysis: the whole clustering fit (all clusters simultaneously), inherited by each candidate

co_assignment_internal_consistency.construct: mean pairwise co-assignment probability among the candidate's own members (Section 9.4 consensus matrix), off-diagonal only
co_assignment_internal_consistency.feasibility_note: requires Section 9.4's co_assignment_matrix, same prerequisite as bootstrap_stability
co_assignment_internal_consistency.min_sample_size: undefined (NaN, not forced) below 2 members -- minimum_cluster_size is the floor-enforcing criterion
redundant_with: cross_algorithm_support (both measure cross-fit agreement, but co-assignment is within-candidate consensus across bootstrap/algorithm resamples while cross_algorithm_support is a single primary-vs-alternative ARI comparison -- different statistical objects, not the same evidence twice)
co_assignment_internal_consistency.unit_of_analysis: member pairs within the candidate cluster

cross_algorithm_support.construct: adjusted Rand index between the primary clustering method's labels and an alternative method's labels, restricted to this candidate's own member rows
cross_algorithm_support.feasibility_note: requires Section 9's CANDIDATE_METHODS (gmm/hierarchical/hdbscan) to have all been fit on the same feature matrix -- a Section 15 discovery-pipeline prerequisite, not a 1.2b-specific gap
cross_algorithm_support.min_sample_size: no explicit floor beyond minimum_cluster_size; ARI itself is more reliable with more members
cross_algorithm_support.unit_of_analysis: candidate cluster's member rows, compared across clustering methods

cross_seed_recurrence.construct: count of distinct seed-runs contributing to the cluster
cross_seed_recurrence.feasibility_note: WP E's design carries seed explicitly on every point (seeds_per_point=6 preferred); directly available
redundant_with: parameter_condition_diversity (both require diversity across independent runs, but seed identity and parameter condition are logically distinct axes -- two runs can share a seed-adjacent condition yet differ in outcome, or share a condition under different seeds; kept separate deliberately, not true redundancy)

distinctness_from_noise.construct: margin between mean within-cluster distance and mean cluster-to-noise distance in feature space
distinctness_from_noise.feasibility_note: only meaningful for a clustering method that produces an explicit noise label (hdbscan); gmm/hierarchical assign every point to a cluster, so noise_indices is legitimately empty and this criterion is undefined (NaN) for those methods -- not a 1.2b-specific gap, a pre-existing property of which discovery method produced the candidate
distinctness_from_noise.min_sample_size: undefined below 2 members or when no noise points exist
distinctness_from_noise.unit_of_analysis: candidate cluster members vs. unclassified/noise points, in the discovery feature matrix

independent_of_single_lineage.construct: no single institutional lineage accounts for more than a bounded fraction of the candidate's members
independent_of_single_lineage.feasibility_note: was NOT safely feasible under the 1.2b joint design as originally documented: raw rule_lineage_id collides across the 576 separate seed-runs WP E produced (see convergence_tests.py's module docstring for the full finding). Fixed by requiring composed keys (convergence_tests.compose_global_lineage_id) for any cross-run pooling -- now feasible, and documented directly on the criterion's own docstring so a future caller cannot miss it.
independent_of_single_lineage.min_sample_size: undefined (NaN) on an empty lineage-id list; default max fraction 0.7
independent_of_single_lineage.unit_of_analysis: institutional lineage identity across candidate members

k_selection_non_privileged_support.construct: the candidate's own k has a defined model-selection metric and is not uniquely the single worst-scoring silhouette among evaluated k's
k_selection_non_privileged_support.feasibility_note: DEFAULT_K_RANGE (1..8) is unchanged by 1.2b; no redesign needed
k_selection_non_privileged_support.unit_of_analysis: candidate's k value vs. the full evaluated k range (Section 9.3's DEFAULT_K_RANGE)

minimum_cluster_size.construct: raw member count -- a floor, not a strength-of-evidence measure
minimum_cluster_size.feasibility_note: trivially available the moment a cluster exists; no dependency on WP E-specific data shape
minimum_cluster_size.min_sample_size: the threshold itself (default 5) IS the minimum sample size this criterion enforces on every other criterion

missingness_strategy_robustness.construct: ARI agreement between the primary missingness-handling strategy's labeling and an alternative strategy's labeling, restricted to candidate member rows
missingness_strategy_robustness.feasibility_note: requires Section 9.1's three preprocess_features strategies to have all been fit-on-train and applied; directly available once the discovery pipeline runs
missingness_strategy_robustness.unit_of_analysis: candidate cluster's member rows, compared across the three Section 9.1 missingness strategies

non_degenerate_cluster_fraction.construct: candidate size as a fraction of the total pooled sample, bounded away from both a vanishing minority and near-total-sample degeneracy
non_degenerate_cluster_fraction.feasibility_note: n_total for 1.2b is WP E's pooled seed-run count (up to 1152 = 576 runs x up to 2 rows/run if V's sub-parts are ever split into separate rows -- confirm the discovery pipeline's own row definition when Section 15 runs; not a criterion-level gap)
non_degenerate_cluster_fraction.min_sample_size: default bounds [0.02, 0.95] of n_total, not a raw count
redundant_with: minimum_cluster_size (different denominators -- criterion 1 is a raw floor independent of pool size, criterion 10 is scale-relative; both matter separately, e.g. a raw-adequate cluster could still be a vanishing fraction of a much larger 1.2b pool)
non_degenerate_cluster_fraction.unit_of_analysis: candidate cluster size vs. n_total pooled observations

parameter_condition_diversity.construct: count of distinct generative parameter conditions represented among the candidate's members
parameter_condition_diversity.feasibility_note: WP E's design point + IC family together define 'condition' cleanly for 1.2b; no redefinition needed from Level 1.2's own usage
redundant_with: cross_seed_recurrence (see that entry's note -- deliberately distinct axes)
parameter_condition_diversity.unit_of_analysis: generative parameter condition (a joint ecological+institutional design point under WP E, or an initial-condition family)

temporal_persistence_of_members.construct: fraction of candidate members whose own seed-run was sustained_system_eligibility-eligible (Section 8B)
temporal_persistence_of_members.feasibility_note: requires each WP E run's own eligibility flag; WP E's own ledger-closure gate (Section 5.7, now satisfied for all 576 runs) is a stricter, DIFFERENT bar than sustained_system_eligibility and does not substitute for it -- eligibility must still be computed per run before this criterion can be applied
temporal_persistence_of_members.min_sample_size: default 0.5 minimum eligible fraction; undefined (NaN) on an empty member-eligibility list
temporal_persistence_of_members.unit_of_analysis: seed-run eligibility, one flag per member's originating run

component_homology_vs_analogy.definition: biology-inspired reframing of inherited/convergent: homology=shared-origin similarity (within-run lineage sharing OR cross-run direct transmission), analogy=independently-arisen similarity (the convergent label)
distinguishes_from: no new computation -- an interpretation layer over the other three levels, recorded explicitly so it is never reinvented ad hoc

cross_run_structural_similarity.definition: members from different seed-runs land in the same discovered cluster -- a purely descriptive, pre-causal observation
distinguishes_from: independent_convergence: this level makes no claim about WHY members are similar, only that they are

independent_convergence.definition: cross-run structural similarity that is ALSO lineage-diverse beyond chance, not majority transmission-linked, and recurs across more than one parameter condition
distinguishes_from: within_run_lineage: requires cross-run evidence, never satisfied by one run alone

within_run_lineage.definition: shared ancestry between institutions in the SAME seed-run
distinguishes_from: cross_run_structural_similarity: different seed-runs, so this level never applies across runs
